content:
Since \(\log_{2026}x\) is involved, \(x>0\). Let

\[
t=\log_{2026}x,
\qquad\text{so}\qquad x=2026^t.
\]

Both sides of the original equation are positive, so raising them to the \(20\)th power preserves equivalence:

\[
x^{\log_{2026}x}=(26x)^{20}.
\]

Substituting \(x=2026^t\),

\[
2026^{t^2}=26^{20}\cdot 2026^{20t}.
\]

Writing \(26^{20}\) as a power of \(2026\),

\[
2026^{t^2}
=2026^{20\log_{2026}26}\cdot 2026^{20t}
=2026^{20t+20\log_{2026}26}.
\]

Thus

\[
t^2=20t+20\log_{2026}26,
\]

or

\[
t^2-20t-20\log_{2026}26=0.
\]

Its discriminant is

\[
400+80\log_{2026}26>0,
\]

so there are two real values of \(t\), hence two possible positive values of \(x\). If the roots are \(t_1,t_2\), then

\[
t_1+t_2=20.
\]

Therefore the product of the corresponding values of \(x\) is

\[
2026^{t_1}\cdot 2026^{t_2}
=2026^{t_1+t_2}
=2026^{20}.
\]

Now

\[
2026=2\cdot 1013,
\]

where \(1013\) is prime. Hence

\[
2026^{20}=2^{20}\cdot 1013^{20},
\]

which has

\[
(20+1)(20+1)=441
\]

positive divisors.

\[
\boxed{441}
\]
